trust_decision.summary: The identity of an observation is decided by computeObservationContentHash: a 16-hex truncated SHA-256 of memorySessionId|title|narrative concatenated with no field boundary, and the dedup query trusts that string as an exact key (content_hash = ?), so two distinct observations whose fields re-split the same character stream are indistinguishable and one is silently dropped.

landing_point.why: The advisory names computeObservationContentHash, and that function exists only here; lines 24-27 hold the whole cause (unseparated concat plus slice(0,16)).

fix_sites.entry_point: POST /api/memory/save; POST /sessions/:sessionDbId/observations (+ /api/sessions/observations alias); exported storeObservation()/storeObservations()/storeObservationsAndMarkComplete(); bin import-xml-observations

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: plugin/scripts/worker-service.cjs:19 and plugin/scripts/context-generator.cjs:9 (minified copies of the same hash: update((t||"")+(e||"")+(r||"")).digest("hex").slice(0,16))

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Both .cjs files are esbuild output bundled from src/services/worker-service.ts and src/services/context-generator.ts (scripts/build-hooks.js:16-27,98-103) and the repo's own build regenerates them, so a solver can argue 'fix the source and let npm run build handle the bundle' - which is also exactly why the shipped copies stay stale unless the fix touches them.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The 30s dedup must keep collapsing genuinely identical repeat observations, and the persisted content_hash is a 16-char value with a non-unique index and pre-existing/backfilled rows; a fix that cuts a full 64-char digest, prefixes a version/scheme marker, or adds a nonce/timestamp to the key either stops dedup from ever matching or orphans every hash already stored, and the existing tests pin hash length at 16.

O6_input_shapes: field-boundary shift between title and narrative: (title="ab", narrative="c") vs (title="a", narrative="bc") hash identically
null vs empty string: (null, null) and ("", "") both normalise to the same input
boundary shift between memory_session_id and title
truncation to a 16-hex (64-bit) prefix of the digest

O7_producer.where: src/services/sqlite/migrations/runner.ts:841 (migration 22 backfills content_hash with substr(hex(randomblob(8)),1,16)); duplicated at src/services/sqlite/SessionStore.ts:853

O8_uncovered_routes.route: POST /api/import stores observations through SessionStore.importObservation, which dedups on (memory_session_id, title, created_at_epoch) and inserts with content_hash NULL, so no content-derived identity is applied on that route at all
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is a restore/import path for an external database dump, not the live write path, it uses an exact-millisecond key of its own, and the advisory only names computeObservationContentHash, so it was never covered.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: another module (worker HTTP routes -> legacy SessionStore import method), 2 files and a package boundary away from the observations store module

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Rows backfilled by migration 22 carry a random 16-hex content_hash that was never derived from their content, so a post-upgrade/save-reload re-insert of an existing observation can never match them
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The backfill comment says the random values are deliberate 'so they don't block new inserts', and SQL cannot recompute a SHA-256 in this schema, so a solver can call it a design choice rather than part of the collision fix.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: migration layer, a different file from the store module and only reachable on an existing database

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A content-hash dedup for session_summaries mirroring the observation one
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Summaries are written by the same worker transaction (transactions.ts:106-127) with no dedup at all, so a maintainer adding duplicate protection would copy computeObservationContentHash and inherit the same unseparated-concat identity.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A content-derived stable vector id for observation chunks instead of obs_${id}_narrative
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The sync layer already needs a deterministic identity to upsert chunks and already imports observation content; hashing title/narrative/facts there is a natural next step and would repeat the same field-boundary ambiguity.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second dedup identity (session+title+exact epoch) for imported observations
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This already exists as a divergent copy of the store path, so a maintainer unifying import with the live path would plausibly bolt the content hash onto it.

O9_family: CWE-327: risky hash construction - truncated digest over an ambiguous, unseparated concatenation used as a dedup identity (silent data loss on collision)

O10_build.toolchain: bun >= 1.0 (bun install, bun test); npm run build = node scripts/sync-plugin-manifests.js && node scripts/build-hooks.js (esbuild bundles into plugin/scripts/*.cjs)
O10_build.project_tests: tests/sqlite/data-integrity.test.ts covers this exact area (hash consistency, null handling, length 16, 30s dedup, content_hash populated); also tests/services/sqlite/migration-runner.test.ts:92-129 and tests/services/sqlite/schema-repair.test.ts. Run with bun test tests/sqlite/.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Hash only the field the report's example varies (narrative) or add a nonce/timestamp so hashes never collide - the visible tests stay green while the identity is still ambiguous or the 30s dedup stops working.
